title: land runs as one job across its merge request: the job waits as waiting-merge without holding a slot or the landing lock, and finishes with the second pass
goal: kj_land.drive(job, run_pass, merged, sleep, post) runs a land job as one job: the first pass is bl_land's land ID --wait-merge 0; when it pushed a code branch its pending (shas, branch) is read with bl_land.pending_merge(root, iid), the job moves to waiting-merge with the branch in the event, the executor's slot and the landing lock are free while it polls merged_on_main every 60 s for up to the wait_merge option (default 1800 s), and when the shas are on the integration main the job moves back to running for the second pass (land ID --wait-merge 0 again, which finishes the item as a content landing) and ends succeeded; a wait that runs out ends refused with step wait-merge and the text land says today (merge it with backlog.py merge ID, then submit again); the job never merges the request itself; a job found in waiting-merge after an executor restart (ST-5cqlfweg) polls again from its recorded pending without running the first pass again; a content landing is one pass and never waits

run: import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"_tools"); import kj_land; ev=[]; calls=iter([False,False,True]); r=kj_land.drive({"job":"JB-x","subject":"ST-1","options":{"wait_merge":600}}, run_pass=lambda second: (0,"ok",None) if second else (0,"pushed code/ST-1",(["abc"],"code/ST-1")), merged=lambda shas: next(calls), sleep=lambda s: ev.append(("sleep",s)), post=lambda state,**f: ev.append((state,f.get("step")))); st=[e[0] for e in ev if e[0]!="sleep"]; assert st==["running","waiting-merge","running","succeeded"], ev; assert sum(1 for e in ev if e[0]=="sleep")==2, ev; assert r==(0,"succeeded"), r

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"_tools"); import kj_land; ev=[]; r=kj_land.drive({"job":"JB-x","subject":"ST-1","options":{"wait_merge":120}}, run_pass=lambda second: (0,"pushed",(["abc"],"code/ST-1")), merged=lambda shas: False, sleep=lambda s: None, post=lambda state,**f: ev.append((state,f.get("step")))); assert r==(1,"refused") and ev[-1]==("refused","wait-merge"), (r,ev)

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"_tools"); import kj_land; seen=[]; def_rp=None; r=kj_land.drive({"job":"JB-x","subject":"ST-1","state":"waiting-merge","pending":{"shas":["abc"],"branch":"code/ST-1"},"options":{"wait_merge":600}}, run_pass=lambda second: seen.append(second) or (0,"ok",None), merged=lambda shas: True, sleep=lambda s: None, post=lambda state,**f: None); assert seen==[True] and r==(0,"succeeded"), (seen,r)

import sys; sys.path.insert(0,"_tools"); import kj_land
ev=[]; polls=[]
r=kj_land.drive({"job":"JB-x","subject":"ST-1","options":{"wait_merge":600}}, run_pass=lambda second: (0,"ok",None), merged=lambda shas: polls.append(shas) or True, sleep=lambda s: None, post=lambda state,**f: ev.append(state))
assert r==(0,"succeeded") and ev==["running","succeeded"] and polls==[], (r,ev,polls)

clauses.clause: kj_land.drive(job, run_pass, merged, sleep, post) runs a land job as one job: the first pass is bl_land's land ID --wait-merge 0

when it pushed a code branch its pending (shas, branch) is read with bl_land.pending_merge(root, iid), the job moves to waiting-merge with the branch in the event, the executor's slot and the landing lock are free while it polls merged_on_main every 60 s for up to the wait_merge option (default 1800 s)
when the shas are on the integration main the job moves back to running for the second pass (land ID --wait-merge 0 again, which finishes the item as a content landing) and ends succeeded
a wait that runs out ends refused with step wait-merge and the text land says today (merge it with backlog.py merge ID, then submit again)
the job never merges the request itself
a job found in waiting-merge after an executor restart (ST-5cqlfweg) polls again from its recorded pending without running the first pass again
a content landing is one pass and never waits

notes: Premise (reproduces today): a code item's land is one command that waits inside the session's call: bl_land.land_pass (bl_land.py:2404) runs pass one, polls wait_merge (bl_land.py:2206, every WAIT_POLL 60 s, bound --wait-merge default 1800) and runs land_once again; the orchestrator's call, or its background shell, is held for all of it. Measured 2026-11-08 from kb/_querylog/ops (real items, 2026-10-02..11-08): wait-merge step median 2.6 s but p90 240 s, p95 458 s, max 1736 s (n=1157); a code landing's land.end median 430 s (n=133, p90 1409 s) against 103 s for a content landing (n=1701); 133 code landings ended exit 0 and 133 exit 1, the exit-1 ones median 168 s (p95 2282 s), many of them the wait-merge stop. Choice: poll in the executor with merged_on_main (read from git, not the forge CLI, as land does), because the executor can hold a thousand waiting jobs for the price of one poll loop, where today each wait holds a process; the job never merges the request: backlog.py merge ID stays the one agent merge (bl_land.py:2462 cmd_merge) and the operator's, the job only reports waiting-merge so the session can run backlog.py merge or tell the operator, then go on. The second pass is the same land command: it already finishes a merged code item as content (bl_land.py:1973 docstring), and the run-state moves landing/landed/refused stay the CLI's (bl_land.py:2378). bl_land.pending_merge reads what LAND_OPS['pending'] holds from git (the code/ID branch pushed and its commits not on the main), so a restarted executor needs no memory. Related drafts: ST-igkt3vsr (wait-merge does not count landing-lock wait, which the executor's queue removes), ST-yh5ivly4 (a request stuck preparing), ST-5l6ldosq (branch gone because it merged), ST-ep7loyre (second pass stops at fetch with no line) share the same step; none is duplicated here. Order 2026-11-08 (ask A1e21b0d155): map.csv, bl_land.py by first claim; rebase.
